title: Products
summary: A catalogue of the things you sell, so quotes and invoices are built by picking rather than typing.
html:
A product is anything you put on a quote or an invoice: a physical item, an hour of a particular kind of work, a recurring service. Keeping them here means consistent wording and consistent prices, and it makes building a quote a matter of picking lines.

Adding one

Products → Create Product. What matters:

  • Name — short, what you would say on the phone.
  • Description — the longer wording that lands on the quote or invoice. Write it for the customer.
  • Price and tax rate.
  • Category, optionally.

Categories

Categories group products so a long catalogue is navigable. Whether the category name is shown alongside the product on a quote or invoice line is controlled by product_show_category_in_tasks.

Suppliers

A product can record which supplier you buy it from, which is useful when a price changes and you need to find everything affected. Suppliers are customer records with the supplier type — see Suppliers and vendors.

Changing a price

Changing a product's price changes it for future quotes and invoices only. Documents already raised keep the price they were raised at, which is the correct behaviour — an invoice must not change under a customer who already has it.

Subscriptions

A product can be set up as something a customer subscribes to rather than buys once. See Recurring invoices and subscriptions.
